Find applicable evidence-backed ways to reduce execution time in this GitHub Actions workflow. Consider its jobs, dependencies, commands, triggers, and repository manifests.
# Upload to PyPI when a GitHub Release is published.
# https://docs.github.com/en/actions/automating-builds-and-tests/building-and-testing-python#publishing-to-package-registries

name: Upload Python Package

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  # Re-run from Actions after workflow fixes (uses the selected branch/ref).
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  deployment:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: publish
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install build tools
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install build

      - name: Build package
        run: python -m build

      - name: Check metadata
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade "twine>=7"
          twine check dist/*

      # hatchling emits Metadata-Version 2.5; Twine 6 rejects it.
      # gh-action-pypi-publish v1.14.2+ ships Twine 7 which accepts 2.5.
      - name: Publish package
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@v1.14.3
        with:
          user: __token__
          password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}

        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
